record_title: Local congruence criterion and three-support rigidity for prime power pseudoperfect numbers
scientific_context: For n=product p_i^a_i, integrality of 1/n plus the reciprocals of every prime-power divisor is equivalent to the local congruences n/p_i^a_i congruent to p_i-1 modulo p_i^a_i. For at most four prime supports these congruences are equivalent to prime power pseudoperfectness. In the three-support slice p^a q r^c with p<q<r and q occurring to exponent one, the unique family is 6*7^c.
limitations: For support size greater than four, the local congruences characterize integrality but do not alone force the reciprocal sum to equal one. The three-support classification assumes the middle-prime exponent is one. Originality is to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk from equivalent formulations under generalized Egyptian-fraction or Sondow terminology. The finite verification supports but does not replace the proofs; no formal proof-assistant verification or independent audit is asserted.

artifact_inventory.description: Standalone exact-rational verification of the local congruence criterion through 100,000 and direct checks of the family 6*7^c.
Deterministic output of the finite verification.
